static_traits.name: Yang Heng
static_traits.family_status: Lives with the spouse, has three children
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with spouse and children due to self-blame and lack of confidence; has a close friend in the same neighborhood to discuss some issues with, but struggles to talk about own inadequacy and inferiority
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness history; no similar psychological problems or psychotherapy experience in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic; somewhat negative mood, with doubt but willing to cooperate; able to describe their own automatic thoughts and emotional experiences

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I am a bad father because the children missed their favorite TV program this afternoon, and I blame myself for it.
basic_info.core_demands: I want to stop always feeling like a failure; I hope to enjoy time with family without persistent guilt.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough/I am a failure

special_situations.event: The children missed their favorite TV show due to a scheduling mistake
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I can't schedule the children's routines perfectly without mistakes, it proves I am an incompetent father
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling planning and scheduling of the children's routines, striving to make no more mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I can't even do such a simple thing well, I am a terrible father

special_situations.event: After the child makes a mistake in an activity, shows disappointment or sadness
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Whenever a child is unhappy it's my fault; a qualified father should keep children satisfied at all times
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately blames himself, over-apologizes, and tries to remedy by controlling more details
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault,I let them down

special_situations.event: The spouse points out they are more irritable and distant, leading to an argument
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as my family isn't satisfied with me, it proves I am utterly useless as a husband/father
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores the things done well, repeatedly picking faults to push oneself to be more perfect
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am incompetent; I do nothing well

special_situations.event: Moments that could be relaxing, such as walking with close friends, are occupied by negative thoughts and hard to enjoy
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I shouldn't enjoy/relax; as long as I haven't perfected the father role, I don't deserve entertainment
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduced socializing and leisure, devoting all time to 'fixing mistakes' and reflection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I don't deserve happiness; I must make up for all my mistakes

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and affirmed by family, loved as a competent, reliable father/husband
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being seen as a failure, disappointing family, and being distanced
defense_goal: Prevents external blame and rejection through self-criticism and pursuing perfection
Strengthening control and planning to reduce uncertainty and the sense of guilt
Creating emotional distance in conflicts to avoid further negation and shame

object_relations.self_representation: The failed/flawed father, the person prone to letting others down
object_relations.object_representation: A child let down by me, ready to be disappointed at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests identifying automatic thoughts or proposes 'behavioral experiments'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that discussing thoughts alone is 'ineffective empty talk'; worth must be proven through perfect behavioral performance
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes logic and evidence in an objective, calm tone, reduces emotional vocabulary, and is reserved and skeptical about suggestions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing failure scenarios like the child missing a program or family dissatisfaction
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing all bad outcomes to myself, ignoring external situational factors (transference: projecting inner harshness onto the self)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly blaming myself, apologizing, using self-deprecating expressions like 'It is all my fault / I am no good'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When noticing others' disappointment or criticism signals (e.g. spouse's complaints, children's displeasure)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Uncritically taking others' 'must be perfect' standards as the only correct rule
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Frequently using 'should/must' self-demanding statements, increasing the intensity of self-control and self-denial.

manifestations: High control and self-blame over father-role responsibilities and choices, worrying each scheduling slip means being unqualified
Tending to constrain myself with perfect standards, afraid of the consequences of making mistakes
outcomes: Rigid perfectionism and high control needs
Family interaction is tense; hard to experience present closeness and relaxation

manifestations: Struggling to discuss own inadequacy and shame with close friends
More irritable and distant with spouse, more arguments
outcomes: Insufficient use of social support, struggling with emotion regulation
Intensified sense of relationship estrangement, self-worth further damaged

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Frequently demands of oneself with 'should / must' to be a perfect father
Treating others' dissatisfaction as an absolute standard to be corrected immediately

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and harsh self-criticism, engaging with others overcautiously.
manifestations: Highly sensitive to own mistakes, repeatedly examining and negating myself
Maintaining skepticism and caution in interactions with the counselor, but still reluctantly cooperating

contact_model.definition: Turns the energy originally meant to be directed outward toward themselves, suppressing expression and the impulse to request support.
manifestations: Converts frustration and anger at the situation into self-blame and self-punishment
Reducing sharing and help-seeking with friends, bearing pressure alone

positive_force: Values family, willing to take responsibility for children
Proactively seeking counseling and willing to try new methods (such as behavioral experiments)
Having some self-awareness, able to identify automatic thoughts and emotions
Has basic social support resources (close friend lives nearby)
Has tried organizing and planning to improve the problem
negative_force: Mental filtering, focuses on negative evidence and ignores the positive side
Irritability and emotional dysregulation worsen family conflict
Shame and isolation make it hard to effectively use social support

antecedent: Mistakes in the children's activities or not yet meeting Anticipation
The child's emotional reaction when disappointed
Thinking of a mistake one made in childcare arrangements
target_behavior.core_reason: The internalized 'perfect father' standard combined with personalization and mental filtering forms a catastrophizing interpretation of mistakes and a devaluation of self-worth
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential blame from others and gains a temporary sense of control and 'responsibility'
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety and guilt worsen, parent-child and marital relationships damaged, rumination cycle continuing

target_behavior.behavior: Easily angered/losing temper with the children
antecedent: Interacting with the children after self-blame and Rising stress
Minor errors in daily family routines
target_behavior.core_reason: Accumulated frustration and shame vented through irritability, accompanied by high demands for order and perfection
target_behavior.function: Briefly releases tension, trying to restore order by controlling others' behavior
target_behavior.consequence: Parent-child conflict escalates and the relationship is damaged, with stronger guilt and self-blame afterward

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids or finds it hard to enjoy leisure / social activities (such as walking with close friends)
antecedent: Having the negative thought 'I do not deserve to enjoy' in leisure settings
Thinking of mistakes not yet 'made up for'
target_behavior.core_reason: The inner belief of 'not deserving to enjoy' and 'should' rules drive self-punishment
target_behavior.function: Through self-restriction, avoids facing self-evaluation and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, decreased pleasurable experiences, Negative emotions persisting
